direct_claims: This chart shows historical estimates of the share of the world's population living on less than $5 per day, by region, from 1820 to 2017.
The data is sourced from the Maddison Project Database, van Zanden et al., and de la Escosura (2020).
The chart is produced by Our World in Data.
The chart measures poverty rates over time, specifically the percentage of the population living on less than $5 per day.

The data is presented by region, including Western Offshoots, Western Europe, Latin America and the Caribbean, Eastern Europe and Central Asia, Middle East and North Africa, India, South Asia excluding India, China, E. Asia and Pacific excluding China, and Sub-Saharan Africa.
The poverty rates shown are lower than corresponding estimates based on survey data.
The chart notes that average incomes measured in national accounts are often much higher than those observed in survey data.
The official estimates produced by the World Bank are used to monitor progress against SDG1.
derived_claims: The trend indicates a significant reduction in poverty over time, with different regions showing varying rates of progress.
